blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Language 3D Gaussian Splatting enables open-vocabulary scene understanding by associating Gaussian primitives with language features. These semantic attributes increase model storage, while most existing 3DGS compression methods are designed mainly to preserve RGB rendering quality. One straightforward approach is to apply sparsification and quantization sequentially. However, pruning based only on rendering quality can remove Gaussians that have small RGB contributions but are important for semantic prediction. Once removed, their semantic information cannot be recovered by later quantization. We propose ClunoGS, a compact framework for Language 3DGS that combines semantics-aware Gaussian sparsification and vector quantization in a unified constrained objective. Semantic supervision is used during sparsification, and the objective jointly considers rendering quality, semantic accuracy, and compactness. We optimize the unified objective with alternating primal, sparsification, quantization, and dual updates. We evaluate ClunoGS on open-vocabulary localization and segmentation using the LERF and ScanNet-10 benchmarks. Under aggressive compression, our unified, semantics-aware formulation substantially alleviates the degradation of semantic representations caused by sequential compression and semantics-agnostic Gaussian sparsification. Ablations further show that jointly coordinating sparsification and quantization better preserves semantic accuracy than applying them independently.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding enables objects in a 3D scene to be
localized or segmented using arbitrary natural-language queries, without
restricting predictions to a predefined class set [ 28 ] .
This capability supports applications such as
AR/VR [ 19 ] , autonomous
driving [ 8 ] , and robotic
manipulation [ 31 , 14 ] . Earlier neural-field methods
encoded semantics in implicit representations, but repeated volumetric
sampling and network evaluation made training and rendering
costly [ 36 , 17 ] . Language 3DGS instead attaches
vision-language features to explicit Gaussian primitives and reuses the
tile-based splatting pipeline of 3DGS to render semantic feature maps
efficiently, avoiding repeated volumetric sampling and per-sample network
evaluation [ 16 , 41 , 30 ] .

Directly attaching high-dimensional vision-language features to individual
Gaussians incurs substantial storage and rendering
overhead [ 41 , 30 ] . LangSplat mitigates this
problem using a scene-specific low-dimensional autoencoder, while LangSplatV2
further replaces the heavyweight decoder with sparse per-Gaussian
coefficients over shared dictionaries, enabling efficient high-dimensional
feature splatting [ 30 , 22 ] . These advances
reduce the cost of semantic feature representation and inference, but do not
target compression of the underlying RGB Gaussian scene. Consequently, a
complete Language 3DGS model still contains the original 3DGS attributes
together with additional semantic parameters. Its compression must therefore
preserve both photometric fidelity and semantic responses.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Language-aware 3D representations lift 2D foundation-model features into
queryable 3D fields, with LERF providing an early NeRF-based
formulation [ 17 ] . Language 3DGS methods mainly follow two
paradigms. Render-supervised methods learn per-Gaussian features or codes by
matching rendered feature maps to 2D supervision, as in LangSplat, Feature
3DGS, GAGS, and LangSplatV2 [ 30 , 41 , 29 , 22 ] . Direct-lifting methods instead register or
aggregate multi-view features onto reconstructed Gaussians without iterative
semantic fitting, as in Dr. Splat and Occam’s
LGS [ 18 , 7 ] . LightSplat and
ExtrinSplat further replace dense per-Gaussian embeddings with compact semantic
indices or an external object-group index [ 2 , 11 ] . We build on LangSplatV2 because its semantic coefficients
and RGB attributes share the same Gaussian support, allowing sparsification and
attribute quantization to account for both rendering and semantic quality.

Recent work has explored compact representations for the semantic features in
Language 3DGS. DF-3DGS separates RGB and semantic Gaussians and sparsifies the
semantic field, while CF3 compresses feature Gaussians through pruning,

CSGaussian progressively entropy-codes both color and semantic
attributes [ 34 ] . SCOUP represents semantic features
with sparse codes, whereas CoSAG predicts and entropy-codes compact semantic
bindings for individual Gaussians [ 4 , 15 ] .
These methods reduce semantic storage through specialized feature
representations and coding schemes.

RGB-only 3DGS compression reduces active primitives, attribute storage, or
bitstream size. GaussianSpa and PUP 3D-GS sparsify optimized scenes using
constrained or uncertainty-based

coding [ 35 , 6 , 32 ] . FCGS applies a

heterogeneous quantization [ 39 ] . ClunoGS instead optimizes
opacity with both RGB and semantic supervision before cardinality projection,
and coordinates Gaussian sparsification with attribute vector quantization in
the same constrained formulation.

blocks.en:

quantization, and dual updates.

Compared with CF3, the smallest competitor on both benchmarks, ClunoGS achieves

It nevertheless ranks second in every semantic and RGB quality metric; its
maximum gaps to LangSplatV2 are only 1.6 mIoU points, 1.1 accuracy points, and
0.07 dB PSNR.
The same trend on both datasets shows that this advantage is not
benchmark-specific.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We present ClunoGS , a unified framework that jointly sparsifies and quantizes
Language 3DGS under RGB and semantic supervision. Across LERF and ScanNet-10,
it substantially reduces storage and peak memory while retaining competitive
RGB and semantic quality. Controlled comparisons show that semantics-aware
selection and primal–dual co-adaptation mitigate the semantic degradation of
sequential compression.
